Case reference: 2014004911.CaseDesc: On July 3, 1974, Ellice Harper, his wife and their young child were out on the lake duck hunting and fishing on Red Sucker Lake, Manitoba. At one point in the day, the party stopped on shore to eat. During this stop, they noticed a storm coming in. By the time they left there were already waves forming as they started out across the lake. The wind increased and the waves were so strong that they would almost cause the vessel to flip over. The boat filled with water and a wave took him out of the boat. His wife and child drifted in the boat until they reached shore and were later rescued. It is presumed Ellice drowned.

Case reference: 2025054353.CaseDesc: On May 8, 1957, William Gatehouse boarded a bus and departed Winnipeg Manitoba, for a personal trip to Las Vegas Nevada, USA. On May 11, 1957, he telephoned his mother to inform her that he was experiencing difficulties in Salt Lake City, Utah. He requested that his brother contact a local lawyer in Winnipeg and arrange for funds to be sent to him in Salt Lake City.  A second call later that day suggested that he had resolved the issue, no longer required the money, and was continuing on his trip to Las Vegas.  There has been no further communication from William.

Case reference: 2014001413.CaseDesc: On September 18, 1959, Captain Charles David Tillsley, Warrant Officer Tyrus Cobb, Sergeant Major James Mackey, and a fourth companion left Fort Churchill on a weekend fishing trip on the Churchill River in Manitoba. They were last seen loading their gear into a boat at the Churchill Dock at around 1 p.m. They were due back on September 20, but failed to return. Fort Churchill's military authorities commenced a search with the aid of helicopters and aircraft. On September 21, the two boats used by the men were located; both were undamaged and swamped. Numerous items belonging to the four men were found. Despite extensive land and water searches, the bodies were not found.

The boat was located two days later, swamped near the Narrows and Popular Point. A search was conducted and lasted for over one month without any success in locating Thomas and Lawrence.

Case reference: 2014001664.CaseDesc: On September 12, 1982, Harold Larcher and his girlfriend set out on Lake Winnipegosis in separate canoes with their supplies from the Overflowing River in Manitoba. His girlfriend's canoe overturned, but she could see that Harold was still in his canoe as she struggled to right her own. She was unable to do so, but at one point she was able to sit on it and eventually made her way to shore, but never saw Harold again. Numerous personal items were recovered, including Harold's passport and a lifejacket that may have belonged to him.  It is presumed that he drowned.
